method.unitOfCount: one remote operation plus its client-side reconciliation path
excluded: loading flags without remote entity duplication
repeated calls to the same operation

labels.avoidable: The remote representation can remain under a server-state owner; the Zustand copy/reconciliation point can be removed.
labels.simplifiable: Some local transition or projection remains useful, but reconciliation can be centralized, replaced by canonical response/cache invalidation, or reduced.
labels.legitimate: The state is primarily a client-owned workflow/UI choice.
labels.inconclusive: Ownership or backend contract is insufficiently clear from repository evidence.

items.operation: query draft -> copy complete response into Zustand
items.reason: The complete remote draft is copied into Zustand; setDraft then manually mirrors draft.cart.products into cart.
items.counterargument: The multi-page flow may need persistence and imperative access, but a server-state cache can provide both without a second mutable representation.

items.operation: save mutation -> copy returned snapshot into draft and cart
items.reason: A canonical mutation response is already available, yet it is copied to a second owner and mirrored by a handwritten store rule.
items.counterargument: Central setDraft reduces caller duplication, although it does not remove the duplicate source of truth.

items.operation: add-transactions mutation -> copy full draft and mirror cart
items.reason: The returned draft is copied into Zustand through a second action that repeats the cart mirroring rule.
items.counterargument: The separate action gives useful devtools semantics but could wrap a canonical cache update instead.

items.entity: draft transactions and product transaction links
items.operation: status-only mutation -> manually remove transactions and clear product links
items.reason: The mutation returns only status, so the client reconstructs all affected representations and must know every derived field to clear.
items.counterargument: A local optimistic projection can avoid a refetch; the risk can still be reduced with an entity-level cache updater and rollback.

items.operation: optimistically null local field -> mutation -> refetch only on failure
items.reason: This is a valid optimistic interaction, but handwritten ownership and rollback are spread across Zustand and a remote refresh helper.
items.counterargument: Optimism is latency-sensitive and cannot be eliminated; only its reconciliation mechanism can be standardized.

items.operation: query configs -> transform array -> copy object into Zustand
items.reason: Server-owned preferences are transformed and hydrated into a global store rather than selected from one server-state owner.
items.counterargument: The object projection is convenient for consumers; it can remain a selector without becoming another mutable owner.

items.operation: update mutation -> ignore response content -> merge request input into Zustand
items.reason: The local state is reconstructed from what the client requested, not reconciled from what the server persisted; new server normalization or derived fields require manual action changes.
items.counterargument: If the mutation contract guarantees exact echo semantics, input-based update may be safe, but that invariant is not encoded locally.

items.operation: viewer query -> format response -> copy to Zustand
items.reason: The fetched collection is server state copied into Zustand after formatting.
items.counterargument: Authentication bootstrap and cross-route availability may justify long cache lifetime, but not necessarily a separate mutable store.

items.operation: health mutation -> apply request variables to patient and allViewers
items.reason: One mutation requires handwritten fan-out to two local patient representations and uses inputs instead of canonical returned patient data.
items.counterargument: The mutation may return only a status, making an optimistic patch reasonable; a normalized single entity would still remove the two-copy fan-out.

items.entity: draft cart products and product details
items.operation: add-product mutation -> merge partial response with existing cart and auxiliary details
items.reason: The operation manually joins response products, existing cart, and request-side metadata, then relies on setDraft to mirror another copy.
items.counterargument: Product category metadata is absent from the mutation response and may legitimately be client-enriched; normalization can centralize rather than eliminate the projection.

items.entity: draft cart, authorizations, and product details
items.operation: status-only remove mutation -> prune products and two dependent collections
items.reason: A single remote removal fans out into manual filters across multiple related local representations; every new dependent representation extends this operation.
items.counterargument: Authorization and display metadata may be local projections, but they should derive from one normalized product set rather than require imperative pruning.

items.operation: save canonical draft -> manually overwrite cart with pre-response products
items.reason: saveDiagnosticDraft already applies the returned snapshot, after which cart is overwritten with the request-side projection, creating a direct hybrid-snapshot risk.
items.counterargument: The overwrite may preserve coupon data omitted by the response, which would expose an API contract gap; it still should be explicit and tested rather than silently replace canonical data.

items.entity: subscription, draft, cart, unit, and payment
items.operation: multi-mutation workflow -> manually assemble final cross-entity store snapshot
items.reason: The workflow legitimately coordinates several remote calls, but final consistency depends on one handwritten object enumerating every affected store representation.
items.counterargument: No single backend response represents the full client workflow, so some orchestration is inherently client-owned.

items.operation: reservation status -> synthesize code on every bookable product in draft and cart
items.reason: A status response is translated into a magic local code and fanned out over two product representations; contract evolution must update this client rule.
items.counterargument: If the API intentionally exposes only reservation status, a local projection is necessary; cache invalidation or a typed projection can reduce risk.

items.operation: remote validation -> copy result into Zustand
items.reason: The async remote result is globally copied and manually coupled to a loading flag instead of being owned by a query result.
items.counterargument: The result may combine several endpoints and business filters, making a composed client cache entry more appropriate than a raw query cache.

items.operation: user selection -> update local workflow state -> synchronize draft/config remotely
items.reason: The immediate selection and derived UI context are client-owned workflow state, although their remote side effects could be consolidated.
items.counterargument: Because draft transactions and preferences persist the choice, the server may ultimately be canonical; repository contracts do not establish a single owner.

items.entity: patient, cloned draft, cart, payment, and config
items.operation: remote clone workflow -> enumerate final store fields and separately persist config
items.reason: After several remote operations, consistency depends on manually listing each affected representation and issuing a separate config update.
items.counterargument: Patient switching is a client transaction spanning backend resources, so orchestration remains necessary even if server-state copies move out of Zustand.

items.operation: authorization query -> split response by type -> copy both collections into Zustand
items.reason: A server response is transformed into two global collections that can be derived from one cached response.
items.counterargument: Downstream pages may need the classification without rerunning the query; a cached selector can satisfy this need.

items.entity: products across cart, selected unit, and units collection
items.operation: remove unavailable products remotely -> manually prune three UI/domain representations
items.reason: One product removal requires coordinated filtering in the store and page-local collection; a missed representation leaves a visually plausible stale unit/product combination.
items.counterargument: The unit search collection is a local view projection and may require an optimistic update, but it can derive from canonical product IDs or use centralized cache updates.

items.entity: currently selected unit and slot-enriched availability
items.operation: select availability result -> store chosen unit globally
items.reason: The raw data is remote, but the identity of the currently selected unit is client workflow state and rooms may be deliberately preserved locally.
items.counterargument: Store only the selected unit ID and derive the full entity from server-state cache, avoiding a mutable copied unit snapshot.
